Alex: heads-up — ran a quick swapbench comparing two attention modes for small-step (decode) workloads, curious if folks see same pattern
Maria: share numbers?
Alex: sure. TL;DR: flash_v2 gives ~12% lower latency on prefill but regresses 8-15% on 1-4 token decode microbatches vs paged_fused. suspect kernel launch path + small-block GEMM overhead
Ben: that matches the perf-bot alert I saw earlier :warning:
perf-bot: alert: decode-latency-spike detected on prod-pool-3, 2026-03-20T14:02Z; bucket=1-4-tokens; p50 up 18%
Satoshi: can you paste the command + perf output?
Alex: posted gist with exact builds but main commands used:
```
# run bench
./bench_attention --model=gptx-small --mode=flash_v2 --seq=1,16 --batch=1,4 --kv_cache=on --profile
./bench_attention --mode=paged_fused --same-args
```
Metrics (median of 5 runs):
flash_v2 decode (1 token): 16.4ms
paged_fused decode (1 token): 14.2ms
flash_v2 prefill (seq=128): 220ms
paged_fused prefill (seq=128): 249ms

Maria: so flash_v2 is faster on long prefill but slower for tiny decode. Do we have kernel launch breakdown?
Alex: yes — profiler shows high % in kernel_launch + small-kernel-setup for flash_v2 during step path. KV cache lookups are fine. stack:
- host scheduling: 1.8ms
- kernel_launch+sync: 8.6ms (flash_v2 decode) vs 6.1ms (paged_fused)
- compute: 5.2ms vs 5.3ms

Ben: interesting — compute is similar but sync overhead kills flash for small batches. Could be stream creation or dynamic workspace allocation.
Satoshi: did you try preallocating workspace / reusing streams?
Alex: yes — enabling stream reuse and static workspace cut kernel_launch by ~2.1ms, brings flash_v2 decode to 14.6ms. Still slightly worse but within noise
Maria: any KV cache interaction? like extra memcpy or stride mismatch?
Alex: KV cache hotpath unchanged. The difference appears only when seq_len small and tokens-per-batch tiny. I suspect different kernel codegen for attention that does extra per-invocation setup in flash_v2 (warp-coop init).
Ben: can we add a fastpath in runtime: route decode microbatches (tokens<=4 && batch<=4) to paged_fused, keep flash_v2 for prefill and larger decodes?
Satoshi: that seems pragmatic. Need to validate memory/correctness for edge-cases. Also add metric tags so console can show route breakdown.
Maria: +1. Also let's add a perf regression alert scoped to small-decode path (new eval prompt set). If quality checks pass, we can do runtime routing first before kernel patch.
Alex: plan: 1) add route heuristic (inference/router.cc) 2) enable stream reuse by default for decode 3) add microbatch eval and dashboard graphs 4) follow up with kernel-level patch to reduce setup cost
Ben: timeline?
Alex: I'll do a quick PR with heuristic + dashboard PR today, run A/B on dedicated pool tomorrow. PR link when up.
perf-bot: note: created perf-ticket #PRF-3421 for small-decode-flash-regression
Satoshi: one more ask — capture nvprof sample for both modes so kernel timestamps can be correlated with our host timeline. put samples in /tmp/bench-samples with run id
Alex: will do. thanks all :rocket:
